analysis:
The PR is documentation-only. docs/reference/configuration.md adds two env-var rows at head lines 415-416: DARKBLOOM_TTFT_STREAM_TOOL_CALLS and DARKBLOOM_TTFT_THINK_CONTENT_SEED. docs/reference/protocol-messages.md adds a paragraph after line 756 describing streamed auto tool-call chunks. No source or control changes are in this batch, and the patch excerpts are complete.

Security-relevant observations (no finding):
- Both env vars are described as default-on and forwarded to the LaunchAgent. The docs describe only incremental, per-call validation of streamed tool calls ("each call is still validated when its frame closes"). The implementing code (ToolStreamPreparation.swift, MLXOpenAIService.swift streamChatCompletionFrames) is not in this batch. So it is unverified that fragments are emitted only inside the existing E2E-encrypted inference_chunk path (T-008, TB-002) and never as plaintext `data` when encryption fails. The docs say `data` is empty when E2E is active, which is consistent with that.
- Tool-call fragments are provider-authored content from an adversarial provider (T-007, ADV-001). Consumers must treat streamed arguments as untrusted until the call is complete. The doc says consumers concatenate fragments by index; the contract that validation occurs only at frame close means partial or invalid arguments may reach consumers earlier than before. This is a behavior change for clients, not a new trust-boundary violation.
- The new TTFT behavior (earlier streaming of content and tool calls) may alter the prefix-cache timing oracle (T-041/SEC-035), but nothing in the supplied docs shows a change to cache hit/miss latency characteristics.
- These env vars are not in the A-008 or attestation-sensitive set. The documented rollback value `0` is trusted-operator local configuration (TB-003).

A future pass should check the implementing source for plaintext fallback on encryption failure and for validation ordering.
